message:
Nathaniel, thank you for replying so quickly. I’ll address each of your questions below.

1. My initial thought was to begin at the start and adapt as much of the story as possible. If you would rather have me concentrate on a particular section, though, I can do that instead.

2. The sample folder I shared shows my usual script style. For every page, I recommend using a panel format. Although I sometimes indicate caption placement, I generally leave the precise positioning of dialogue balloons and similar elements to the artist.

3. Because I would be adapting your script, I would shape the pacing and structure mainly by choosing how many panels, or how much page space, each moment receives. Those decisions should be reasonably self-explanatory, but I can explain them after writing if you would like. Including explanatory notes would require additional time, which would also raise my rate for the larger project.

I look forward to your response.

While I continue evaluating all candidates next Monday, I’ll hold off on a final choice and make my decision by noon (my time). Thank you for the excellent response, and please send over any questions you may have.

Dom,

I have one last question: how much time would you need to complete this sample project?

Thanks!
Nate

My target would be to return the script by the following Thursday, provided I can begin next Monday. That schedule would leave a gap between the first and second drafts while also reserving time to address any questions that arise.

Thanks,
Dom

The 18-page sample is something I’d like to move forward with. Let me know if you accept, and I’ll send the contract under the terms already discussed in our messages. Please raise any questions you have; otherwise, I’ll send it out shortly. Thanks!

For additional context, I’ve attached several other files. If you need more material or have any questions, just let me know. I’m available throughout the day and, when necessary, at night as well. Thanks!

Because the project appears to have already been funded, I’ll get started in the early afternoon. I’ll contact you if any questions arise, and regardless, I’ll try to provide an update by midday next Tuesday.

Today’s progress has been good: I’ve drafted a tentative breakdown that reaches Tom’s meeting with Apollonia on comic page 18. As I continue, I may find that this pace is too brisk if some beats require more room to breathe.

Before proceeding further, I want to check two questions—or, more accurately, two thoughts about the script—with you:

1.. In several places, I may adapt portions of the scene descriptions into "voice over" caption text.

2\. To use the available page space efficiently, I may omit a few brief exchanges. One example is at the bottom of page 41, where Carter tells Tom that he is invited to the dinner shown in the following scene.

Would deviations of this size be acceptable, or should the comic reproduce the screenplay line-for-line? Let me know what you think.

Thanks.

Dom,

Because this is a sample piece, you have carte blanche and I’ll defer to your judgment. Let me know if there is anything you need from me.

Nate
For the entire afternoon on Friday, I’ll be away from my desk. Even with that limited availability, I’ll answer any questions as soon as I can.
The work looks great. I’ll contact you if anything else is needed, but would you be comfortable leaving the contract open a little longer? Please let me know. Thanks!
At this stage, the job can simply remain open.

Dom,

Could you provide a total quote for 96-102 pages?

Thanks!
Nate

To work out how much time this would require, could you tell me how many episodes or screenplay pages the 102 comic
pages should cover? I’m glad to hear from you again.

The original book contains 8 parts, and I’m considering the first four parts for the initial graphic novel. I can send you the relevant files tomorrow morning. Production costs are still being finalized, and the crowdfunding campaign is scheduled to launch on Thursday, so I’d appreciate receiving your quote two days beforehand. Thanks!

To calculate the estimate, I’ll review both the files already in my possession and anything else you send. I’ll aim to deliver the estimate tomorrow
afternoon; if I cannot, you’ll have it next Wednesday.

Using what I had already written, I worked through the numbers.

First, could you clarify whether the request is for 102 pages of screenplay or 102 pages of comic? My completed work produced an approximate screenplay-to-comic conversion of roughly 3:1.

If part 4 is approximately the same length as episode 1, then parts 1 through 4 should amount to around 54-60 comic pages. I could complete that scope for $625 with a turnaround of 5 weeks. If I can reuse 18 pages from the sample script with only light revision and page reflowing, I could reduce that price to $475.

The larger option of 96-102 comic pages is also possible, but it would require covering more of the story, presumably through episode 5 or 6. For that scope, I propose $1125 with a 7-week turnaround. With 18 pages of the sample script reused, the price would instead be $950.

Please let me know which option is closer to what you have in mind and whether these terms work for you.

Thanks,
Dom

The current estimate is for 102 pages of comic. I’ve attached the next five scripts, and I believe you also received a version of the novel earlier. Since that version is divided into six sections, it may serve as a better source than the scripts. Please review everything and tell me what you think.

For this service, I have budgeted $2400. Although I appreciate your earlier quote, that amount seems more appropriate compensation for your time. Send me any questions you have, and I’ll update you when there is news. Thanks!

Thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote more time to finding the best way to present everything instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Should I begin in three weeks, or wait until you explicitly say "go?"

I can commit to scripting 96-102 comic pages. After reviewing the next five episodes and the novel, I’ll determine how much of the story fits within that space. While doing so, should I pace the adaptation with the eventual remainder of the story in mind? In other words, should this section feel self-contained, or should it leave readers asking, "What’s next?"

Thanks,
Dom
The listing is scheduled to be posted on Friday. Would you object if I used your name and identified you as the project’s scripter, or by whichever title you prefer?

You have my permission, and my preferred credit is Dominic Hale.

If you want to avoid other bidders, either of us can create the next job as a follow-up to this one.
A milestone will be added, but the plan is still to fund this through Kickstarter, so the outcome remains uncertain. Fingers crossed.
Is this portion of the job therefore conditional on receiving funding through Kickstarter?
That is correct, and I thought the contingency had been clear. Does knowing this alter your involvement?

I had understood that this work would help secure crowdfunding, rather than that payment for the work itself was not yet funded. Unfortunately, I cannot accept speculative work through this site. The job is also too large for me to undertake on that basis even if the site allowed it.

Sorry for the confusion. I’m still hoping to obtain funding, and the sample I paid for was part of that effort. The project will move forward if the campaign succeeds, but I’m not requesting any additional work from you yet. If you prefer to withdraw from future involvement, please tell me as soon as possible.

It seems I misunderstood, and I apologize if my response was short. Once the funding is ready, I’ll be happy to proceed with the work; until then, I can delay starting while you run the Kickstarter campaign. Best of luck, and I hope to hear that it succeeds.
When the campaign goes live, I’ll share its link. You’re also welcome to send me a short bio for the listing, but that is entirely optional.

The campaign link is below. Its pre-launch is next Tuesday, followed by the full launch on Saturday. Please feel free to share it.

<https://www.kickstarter.example/projects/moonlit-press/clockwork-islands-book-one>
Thank you—this is exciting. Wishing the campaign every success.

The campaign did not perform as well as I had hoped. I appreciate your participation, effort, and time, but I’ll be closing the contract next Thursday. You will, of course, receive a top-notch review from me.
That’s disappointing to hear. Working with you has been a pleasure, and I wish you every success with your future projects. If you need another writer later, please keep me in mind.

Dom,

The artist scheduled for this project has offered to produce additional artwork gratis and would like me to run the kickstarter again. Unless you object, I’ll keep the contract open rather than close it. I’ll update you whenever anything changes.

Nate
Keeping the contract open is no problem. I’ll continue watching for updates, and please contact me if you need anything else.

Dom,

There isn’t much new information to share right now. I’m currently considering a timeline that would have the campaign launched again by the middle of September.

Thanks again for your help!
Nate
With the project now on hold until further notice, I’m going to end the contract. Thank you for your time; I’ll leave excellent feedback, and if you ever need anything, please let me know.
